scope: Bounded discovery of Lithuanian legal publication and reuse, EU/EEA/EFTA/Swiss and UK Withdrawal Agreement routes, free movement and third-country family residence, application forms, visa practice and missions, civil-status evidence, administrative procedure and access, remedies, privacy, oversight, legal aid, and administrative courts. This is not a complete national inventory or a legal-equivalence opinion.
retrieval_status: 13 TAR API records and 2 HTML pages converted; one court-search surface captured; 28 direct requests returned HTTP 403 or had no API version row; no source accepted

comparison_seed.source: Danish EU free-movement residence regulation and official guidance
comparison_seed.relationship_note: Lithuania's Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and its residence-card procedure orders have a close functional relationship to the Danish seed for EU citizen and family residence, but use a different statutory structure and distinct EFTA/Swiss and mobile-Lithuanian routes. No legal equivalence is asserted. UK Withdrawal Agreement beneficiaries remain a separate route.

previous_findings_carried_forward: The author-source-pack-rules Denmark-to-Sweden/Finland smoke and earlier country registers are search leads only; Lithuania was verified through Lithuanian first-party publishers.

Carry Czechia's e-Sbírka experience forward as an adapter lesson: check registration and terms before selecting an API, and seek a documented official stable-document route where registration is unavailable.

Carry Estonia, Finland, France, and Germany forward as route-validation lessons: a structured endpoint, open dataset, or RSS description is not proof of live access, coverage, currentness, or conversion quality.
Carry Greece and Hungary forward as a reminder to inspect exact publisher terms and reuse conditions for each endpoint; do not transfer another country's reuse conclusion to Lithuania.

Search law, operational guidance, forms, visa and mission practice, procedure, file access, remedies, family-status evidence, privacy, oversight, legal aid, and courts separately. N-Lex is a law-portal lead, not a complete national inventory.
